subject: Decision Making
title: Wikipedia's Collective Knowledge
description: A quick win: understand Wikipedia's Collective Knowledge.

hook.text: Wikipedia has no central authority. Millions of strangers write and edit articles. It should be chaos. It works.

buildup.text: Studies found Wikipedia's accuracy comparable to Encyclopaedia Britannica on science topics. Crowds matched experts.

discovery.text: Errors get corrected fast. Vandalism is reverted in minutes. The crowd self-polices through norms and vigilant editors.

twist.text: Wikipedia's weakness is obscure topics with few editors. Crowd wisdom requires a crowd. Small groups are easily biased.

climax.text: Wikipedia succeeds because edits are transparent, reversible, and open.

punchline.text: Millions of strangers, one encyclopedia. Structure turns chaos into knowledge.

quiz.question: What makes Wikipedia work despite having no central authority?
options: Transparent, reversible edits and self-policing norms turn contributions into reliability
